nodes.question: What percentage of the SPL is currently recycled or reused according to International Aluminium?
nodes.answer: 40 to 50 percent of the SPL is recycled or reused today.
nodes.paragraph: According to International Aluminium [8]40 to 50 pct of the SPL is recycled/reused in other processes today, where rst cutis mainly used for energy purposes in the production of cement, steel and mineral wool. Second cut SPL is also used for cement production. In all cases the rst cut SPLhas replaced fossil coal or coke. For both cement and steel, the substitution has given an environmental bene t for both industries. Further, for steel making, a costbene t has also been seen. From the examples given byInternational Aluminium, both the aluminum industryand the end-users can bene t both environmentally and economically from developing cost-e ective alternatives to deposit in land Ils. Several methods for puri cation of SPL have been investigated in literature. Chen et al. [13] ]proposes a method named oxidation-expansion acid leaching (OEAL) which is a novel leaching process for removalof impurities inside graphitized carbon. They suggest that the OEAL manages to remove up to 99 pct of the electrolyte remains in the SPL, as compared to 89 pctwhen using conventional leaching. Rio Tinto has devel-oped a method called the low-caustic leaching and liming process (LCL&L), and this process is industrial- ized today.

nodes.question: What factors influence the amount of SPL generated at aluminum producing sites?
nodes.answer: The amount of SPL generated can vary depending on the lifetime of the cells, the design, the degree of cleaning before and sorting during deconstruction, and the degree of reuse of the steel casing.
nodes.paragraph: The worn-out cathode lining is termed as spent potlining (SPL). It is estimated that ca. 25 kg of SPL is generated for everymetric ton aluminum produced. [7]however, this number can vary between aluminum producing industrial sites depending on the lifetime of the cells, the design, the degree of cleaning before and sorting while deconstruct-ing a spent cell, and the degree of reuse of the steel casing. The estimated global yearly production of SPL was around 1.42 million metric tons in 2020 and theestimated forecast in 2050 is 1.85 million metric tons. nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Recycled steel and aluminum_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is primary aluminum metal considered as besides being a valuable product?
nodes.answer: Primary aluminum metal can also be considered as a power bank, as it can be recycled endlessly using a fraction of the energy needed for producing primary aluminum.
nodes.paragraph: Primary aluminum metal is a valuable virgin product but can also be considered as a power bank as it can berecycled endlessly using only a fraction of the energy when remelting compared to the electrochemical reduc- tion of alumina to producing primary aluminum metal. McGeer et al. [16]patented in 1958 a distillation method for recovering material from the aluminum reduction cell lining using high temperature and vac-uum. A distillation column was proposed, where the uorides and metallic sodium are volatilized. A succes- sively lower temperature as the vapors ascends the distillation column will allow the uorides to condensein the rst part of the path and sodium will stay in the vapor phase. In the upper part of the distillation column, the temperature will be low enough for sodiumto condense, away from the uorides. In this method the SPL does not need to be ground to very small particles prior to treatment which is an advantage as grinding istime consuming and costly in terms of investment, labor and energy demand. The foreseen end products would be sodium, cryolite and a puri ed carbon material ( rstcut SPL).

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does increasing the silicon content in steel affect its magnetic properties?
nodes.answer: Increasing the silicon content significantly improves the steel's magnetic properties, enabling rapid magnetization and demagnetization while reducing energy losses associated with hysteresis and eddy currents.
nodes.paragraph: Further, the precise knowledge of the nal solidi cation point plays a particularly impor-tant role in guaranteeing the quality of Si steels. Forboth the secondary metallurgy and casting process, the binary Fe-Si system represents the basis for thermody- namic data for process modeling, e.g., enthalpy data for temperature modeling in secondary metallurgy [7]and phase transformations temperatures required for solid- i cation simulations [8,9] The objective of the present study is to obtain new experimental data on melting equilibria and solid-state transformations at typical Si contents of electrical steel, and higher. Di erential scanning calorimetry (DSC) landhigh-temperature laser scanning confocal microscopy (HT-LSCM) are employed to characterize the phase transformations in the temperature range of 600 to1550 /C176C. In total, 9 alloys are prepared by high-fre- quency remelting (HFR) and spin casting technique carried out under Ar 5N (purity 99.999 pct) atmosphere.High-purity starting materials are used, and Si is alloyed in the composition range of 0.50 to 12.50 wt pct. Based on the new ndings, the thermodynamic system isreassessed over the entire alloy range, whereby the modeling of the individual solution phases is partly adopted from the literature.
